title: Daily math research — arXiv announcement batch, Mon 19 Oct 2026
global_caveat: This is an inferred editorial selection, not an official arXiv trending chart. The papers are new, and reliable citation or attention histories are sparse; the order should not be read as a popularity ranking. All results remain preprint claims pending expert review.

sections.title: Near optimal gap in the Lonely Runner Conjecture
sections.abstract: For every finite set of n ≥ 2 distinct positive integer speeds, the authors prove a uniform lower bound ML(V) > (1+c)/(2n) for an absolute c > 0, improving the basic 1/(2n) bound.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove a positive absolute relative improvement over 1/(2n), using a refinement of a large-GCD argument and a new interval-multiplicity spillover inequality.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: V is any set of n ≥ 2 distinct positive integers; the exact Lonely Runner conjectured threshold 1/(n+1) is not proved.
sections.unique_caveat: The constant c is absolute and explicit in the paper, but the authors do not optimize it; the result remains short of the conjectured bound.

sections.title: Brennan's Conjecture and the Universal Integral Means Spectrum
sections.abstract: The authors present a shorter proof of a stronger statement after checking recent preprints claiming Brennan's conjecture and a broader conjecture of Kraetzer; they say much of the earlier argument can be removed.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim a drastically shorter proof of a significantly stronger statement than the cited recent proofs; the abstract says the broader context and consequences are deferred to follow-up work.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Brennan's claim concerns area integrability of derivatives of conformal maps from simply connected proper plane domains, for exponents 4/3 < p < 4; this note focuses on the proof and universal integral-means spectrum.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a short, unrefereed note that explicitly sacrifices context and consequences; treat the theorem as the authors' preprint claim, not as peer-reviewed consensus.

sections.title: Sharp maximum estimates for linear uniformly elliptic equations with measurable coefficients
sections.abstract: The authors claim sharp exponents for Aleksandrov–Bakelman–Pucci maximum estimates with measurable coefficients, proving Pucci's 1966 conjecture and giving a further sharp formulation for higher-dimensional uniform ellipticity.
sections.claimed_result: For trace-normalized ellipticity in dimensions n ≥ 3, the stated maximum estimate holds for every p above Pucci's proposed critical exponent; the paper also gives a sharp threshold under the standard eigenvalue-ratio formulation.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Linear nondivergence-form uniformly elliptic equations, measurable symmetric positive-definite coefficient matrices, and the Sobolev/continuity class stated in the paper; the estimates apply on finite-volume open sets without boundary regularity.
sections.unique_caveat: The threshold depends on the chosen formulation of uniform ellipticity, and the claimed result is still a new, unrefereed preprint.

sections.title: Height of minimal surfaces: sharp thresholds
sections.abstract: The authors identify sharp aperture thresholds for proper holomorphic curves and describe distinct volume-growth regimes for stationary integral varifolds near the borderline of linear height growth.
sections.claimed_result: For stationary integral varifolds, narrow cones of aperture ε force polynomial volume growth with exponent n+O(ε²), while wide cones permit arbitrarily fast growth; the ε² order is shown sharp in R³.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Proper holomorphic submanifolds and stationary integral varifolds under height/aperture conditions; the holomorphic-curve thresholds also depend on the plane's Kähler angle.
sections.unique_caveat: The geometric conclusions are conditional on those regularity and cone/height hypotheses; the abstract does not make a universal claim about arbitrary minimal surfaces.

sections.title: Disproof of Wright's Problems 14 and 15 on lacunary maximal functions
sections.abstract: The authors disprove two proposed weak-endpoint bounds by constructing a compactly supported singular probability measure with Fourier decay and showing the associated maximal operator has infinite weak-L¹ and H¹-to-weak-L¹ norms.
sections.claimed_result: For every d ≥ 1, the authors exhibit a fixed compactly supported singular probability measure with Fourier decay of every order 0 < ε < 1/2 for which both stated endpoint operator norms are infinite.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The result concerns dyadic convolution maximal operators and the specific weak-L¹ and H¹ endpoint bounds posed in Wright's Problems 14 and 15.
sections.unique_caveat: It refutes those endpoint bounds; it does not settle other lacunary maximal-function estimates or remove the paper's specific measure/operator setup.

sections.title: Analyticity of the correlation length in subcritical FK-percolation and Potts models
sections.abstract: The authors prove that the correlation length is analytic throughout the subcritical parameter regime for FK-percolation and Potts models on the lattice Z^d.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish analyticity of the correlation length throughout the subcritical phase, using the leading eigenvalue of the FK–Ruelle operator and analytic perturbation theory; they also derive a restriction on rotational invariance.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: FK-percolation and Potts models on Z^d, restricted to the subcritical parameter regime.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is confined to the subcritical phase; the abstract does not address criticality or supercritical regularity.
